answer: AI agent networks can resist Sybil attacks via proof-of-work, requiring each agent to solve a complex cryptographic puzzle. This mechanism demands a verifiable computational investment, tying identity to a scarce resource. An attacker seeking to proliferate fake identities would confront an overwhelming, economically infeasible computational burden, akin to diverting an entire river. The difficulty adjusts dynamically, making the required effort as precisely defined as quartz, effectively creating an economic gale against large-scale identity fabrication.
